audit.report: The checkout system degraded after a card settlement worker (pid 129417) entered an idle transaction, blocking 12 sessions and causing 27 timeouts in the first 15 seconds. The business tolerated up to 60 seconds of degradation, but revenue was at roughly $13,382/min at risk. After two negotiation rounds, both guardians agreed to wait for the settlement to complete naturally, which finished on its own after 11 seconds. The verifier confirmed full recovery: all locks cleared, checkout SLO returned to 100%, and the protected settlement operations remained intact.
audit.root_cause: A protected card settlement worker (pid 129417) became an idle transaction blocker, locking out checkout sessions.
lessons: The protected_settlement workload is marked never_interrupt and non-replayable; any future negotiation must check db.protected_settlements and biz.change_calendar before proposing termination.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly identified the protected settlement policy and the 60s business tolerance, but the continuity_guardian had to request two separate evidence items (change_calendar and protected_settlements state) before signing off, adding two rounds to the process.
follow_ups: Add db.protected_settlements and biz.change_calendar checks to the database_guardian's standard lock-graph probe template.
Define a 20s abort threshold for idle protected settlements in the orchestrator's candidate-action enumeration.
Brief the payments owner on the never_interrupt policy and the cost of delayed settlements so they can pre-emptively flag long-running batches.
